title: Visualizing Vectors
teaches: Definition of a vector as a directed line segment with magnitude and direction.
visual: A 2D coordinate grid appears. A point labeled 'P' is plotted at (3, 4). An arrow animates from the origin (0,0) to P. The components '3i + 4j' appear next to the arrow.
narration: In linear algebra, a vector is not just a number but a quantity with both magnitude and direction. We represent it graphically as an arrow pointing from the origin to specific coordinates in space.

title: Vector Addition
teaches: The head-to-tail method of vector addition.
visual: Two vectors, A (red) and B (blue), appear. Vector B animates so its tail touches the head of A. A new green vector C appears connecting the start of A to the end of B, labeled 'A + B'.
narration: Vectors can be combined through addition using the head-to-tail method. By placing the tail of the second vector at the head of the first, the resultant vector connects the starting point to the final endpoint.

title: Scalar Multiplication
teaches: How scalars change magnitude and direction.
visual: A single black vector V is shown. A slider labeled 'k' appears. As k increases from 1 to 2, the vector stretches double its length. As k becomes -1, the vector flips direction but keeps the same length.
narration: Multiplying a vector by a scalar changes its magnitude. If the scalar is positive, the direction remains the same; if negative, the vector points in the exact opposite direction.

title: Linear Combinations
visual: Two orthogonal basis vectors i (red) and j (blue) are fixed. A third vector v (green) appears, dynamically decomposing into components along i and j, showing v = 2i + 3j.
narration: Any vector in a 2D plane can be expressed as a linear combination of basis vectors. This means we can build any vector by scaling and adding the fundamental unit vectors of the coordinate system.
